_readme: Committed trigger-accuracy floors. The build fails when a run drops below one of these.
Floors sit roughly 10 points below the observed value recorded in `observed`, which is the
headroom that 3-vote majority scoring leaves. Single-pass scoring had a 3-point run-to-run
spread on an unchanged corpus; majority voting is what makes a hard floor honest rather than a
coin flip. Do not tighten a floor to the observed value — the next green run becomes luck.
When a floor is breached the fix is almost always the skill's `description` and `when_to_use`,
`negativeRejectionRate` has the least headroom on purpose. A skill that fires on a Kubernetes
question is worse than one that occasionally misses its own topic: it displaces the answer the
user wanted and burns their context on a procedure that does not apply.

knownWeakness.backstage-auth: Both the lowest precision (0.89) and the lowest recall (0.73) in the set, and the floor-setter for each. Its misses are adjacent rather than wrong: definitional questions ("what is CIMD") are judged to need no skill, and "everyone gets logged out after we changed the ingress" goes to backstage-incident-debug, which has a defensible claim on it. Tightening further risks pulling genuine incidents away from incident-debug, which is the more expensive error.
knownWeakness.backstage-kubernetes: One negative still triggers it — a pod OOMKill question. The when_to_use now says explicitly that debugging workloads is cluster operations and out of scope, which moved precision from 0.86 to 0.92; the remaining case is a genuine judgement call about where a Kubernetes question stops being a Backstage question.
